report.source_text: Meningitis started occurring more frequently and was accompanied by sudden brownish urine and occasionally by altered consciousness, which lasted for several days. At the age of 68, the patient developed severe haemolysis. Haemoglobin declined to 8.2 g/dL and lactate dehydrogenase elevated up to 3004 IU/L. He also developed acute renal failure because of the deposition of haemosiderin in renal tubules. Serum creatinine increased from 2.8 to 8.65 mg/dL. He required temporary haemodialysis for a month until his condition improved.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old man had recurrent aseptic meningitis with neutrophilic CSF pleocytosis, urticaria, and arthralgia over 18 years. Infectious and common autoinflammatory genetic causes were ruled out. Later, he developed clinical hemolysis with anemia, elevated LDH, brownish urine, and acute renal failure requiring dialysis. Flow cytometry confirmed deficiency of CD55 and CD59 on erythrocytes and granulocytes, confirming PNH. Molecular testing found a germ-line PIGT nonsense mutation with somatic deletion in chromosome 20q including PIGT. He was treated with eculizumab, leading to complete remission of meningitis, urticaria, arthralgia, headache, and hemolysis symptoms over 3 years.
